verdict.rationale: iTerm2 has a built-in LLM chat window that can link to sessions, run commands on your behalf, and explain output. A hands-on user reports prompting it in plain language to generate an awk command. It is an optional plugin that requires your own API key, and the evidence covers shell-command help rather than natural-language control of iTerm2 itself. missing for 10: evidence of natural-language control of iTerm2's own features (panes, profiles, settings), first-party docs detailing the command-execution behavior, and out-of-the-box availability without a separate plugin and user-supplied API key.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Built-in LLM chat window that can optionally interact with terminal contents. Link sessions to get context-aware help, run commands on your behalf, or explain output with annotations.
This is an optional component you can install to enable generative AI features in iTerm2.
One user prompted the iTerm2 AI feature to use awk to filter the 2nd and 5th columns of piped input and truncate the 5th to 25 chars.
